new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE CHECK. (+.txt, and = p.1211): Table 1 'Principal phonetic distinguishing features of Admiralty Islands languages' rows read exactly (Group 1 | Group 2 | Group 3): 'main position of accent | penultimate | initial | final'; 'rhythm | stress-timed | syllable-timed | mixed type'; 'tones | - | - | + in some dialects' (txt lines 257-262, image verified by eye). p.1214 (txt l.437), Group 3, Subgroup B, I, 'Family 2. a. Levei, Lindro, Banum, Drehet, Malai'. Every quoted word is present at the stated locators; the only differences are the first reader's bracketed table-linearisation glue ('[Table 1, row]', '[Group 1]' etc.), hence 'minor differences'. Blust RB2-011 packets also re-read: p.285…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Smythe assigns 'final' as the main position of accent to his whole Group 3 (Manus and adjacent islands, some 25 languages), which includes Levei and Drehet; this is a group-level table cell, not a description of Khehek. Blust's 1975 Ndrehet field transcriptions (RB2-011 pp.285-295, on file) mark stress overwhelmingly on the initial syllable (penult in disyllables, antepenult in trisyllables), with final marks mainly on glottal-final or 3sg-suffixed forms, so the only primary evidence points the other way.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing in Smythe. Blust's Ndrehet notes occasionally write a grave (secondary) on a later syllable, e.g. púrikòhuN.
new_statements.exceptions: None in Smythe (table cell only; 'tones: + in some dialects' for Group 3).
new_statements.domain_note: Smythe: unspecified (impressionistic group typology). Blust fieldnotes: isolated citation forms elicited from one teenage speaker per variety.
new_statements.identity_note: kheh1237 Khehek = Levei + Drehet (Ndrehet) [+ Bucho/Pujou] of west-central Manus; older sources (Smythe 1970, Schooling 1988, Ross 1988) fold it into 'Levei-Tulu (Keli)', whose Tulu half is now Tulu-Bohuai (tulu1259, ISO rak). Blust's packets are village-specific: packet 8 = Levei dialect, packet 19 = Ndrehet (Drehet) dialect. Smythe's accent cell is for his entire Group 3 (all Manus languages), not for Khehek.
